newsitem.title: HONG KONG: World Bank plans stake in China's Minsheng Bank.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans stake in China's Minsheng Bank.

text.p: The World Bank intends to take a small stake in China's first privately-run bank, but the supranational giant has yet to see the final terms, a senior World Bank officer said on Monday in Hong Kong.

Richard Frank, managing director of the World Bank and chairman of its Private Sector Development Group, said the bank's private sector financing arm, the International Finance Corp (IFC), was planning to take a stake in Minsheng Bank.
"It is one of the highest priorities of our advising and investing in China," Frank said.
"We are looking for all ways possible to build deeper domestic financial markets," he said in a speech to the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce.
China Minsheng, the nation's first non-state bank since 1949, was set up in January 1996 in Beijing with a registered capital of 1.38 billion yuan (US$166 million) put up by 59 companies.
The scope of the bank's business is quite small -- in the first six months of 1996, the bank's two branches had combined deposits of 2.23 million yuan and assets of 3.68 million yuan.

However, it ambitiously aims to raise its capital to 5.0 billion yuan and its deposits to 3.5 billion yuan during its first year of operation, while extending its branch network to Shanghai, Guangzhou, and other coastal cities as well as Chengdu in Sichuan province.
Hong Kong newspapers reported the World Bank aimed to take a 10 percent stake in Minsheng, but Frank said the details had not yet been worked out.
Frank said the World Bank's aim is to assist China in building a credible private banking system.
"When we are there as an investor I think that we are actually then in a better position to be an advisor," said Frank. "This has been a pattern for us in many countries."

"If there are banking policies or government regulations which are constraining the growth of the banking system, we can advise governments from our more general perspective...but also from the point of view of having been an investor so it makes us much more credible even as a advisor, he added.
If and when the World Bank takes a stake in Minsheng, it will take a seat on the board of directors, Frank said.

"We are not there principally as a large shareholder, but principally as a minority investor to help build the operating policies, build the operating style, and that comes in part by putting someone on the board of directors," he explained.
The World Bank would sell its stake to domestic investors once Minsheng was mature, and would be seeking a return on its investment of 15 percent, Frank said.

He said the World Bank was considering other investments in banks and other financial institutions involved in areas such as leasing, investment finance and housing finance, but would not be drawn on whether the bank would invest in CITIC Industrial or other Chinesequasi-state banking institutions.
Frank said the World' Bank's development group had 150 private sector investments in financial institutions around the world. (US$1=8.3 yuan)
